title: Completion popup: state model + reducer transitions + scenario test (no UI yet)
description:

Following the discipline that broke WS-13: state is the single source of truth; UI is a function of state; keyboard handlers are scoped to popup-Open state only.

Implementation:
1. New module 'src/services/completion_popup.rs':
   pub enum CompletionPopupState {
       Hidden,
       Open {
           anchor_offset: usize,                // caret offset where popup anchors
           items: Vec<CompletionPopupItem>,
           selected_index: usize,
       },
   }
   pub struct CompletionPopupItem {
       pub display_text: String,
       pub insert_text: String,
       pub kind: CompletionPopupKind,           // mirrors CompletionProposalKind
       pub replacement_span: Option<FormulaTextSpan>,
       pub documentation_ref: Option<String>,
   }
   pub enum CompletionPopupKind { Function, DefinedName, TableName, TableColumn, StructuredSelector, SyntaxAssist }
2. State slot: add 'pub completion_popup: CompletionPopupState' to FormulaSpaceState; default Hidden.
3. Reducer entry points in 'src/app/reducer.rs':
   - sync_completion_popup_with_proposals(state, anchor_offset, items): transitions Hidden -> Open if items non-empty AND user activity warrants it; transitions Open -> Hidden if items empty; preserves selected_index when items list is the same shape.
   - move_completion_selection(state, delta): wraps within bounds when popup is Open; no-op when Hidden.
   - dismiss_completion_popup(state): forces Hidden.
   - accept_selected_completion(state) -> Option<CompletionAcceptance>: returns the accepted item's replacement_span + insert_text + new caret offset; transitions to Hidden. Returns None when popup is Hidden.
4. Auto-open policy (called from apply_live_editor_input): after every bridge round-trip, sync_completion_popup_with_proposals is called with editor_document.completion_proposals. The first wave's policy: open whenever proposals are non-empty (regardless of trigger char). A future bead can refine to alphanumeric/'='/('('/'.' triggers only.
5. Auto-close policy: any input event whose proposal list is empty -> Hidden. Any focus-out (handled later via DOM event) -> Hidden.

Test scaffolding (state-side, all unit-testable without browser):
- Reducer unit tests covering EVERY transition:
  * Hidden + non-empty proposals + trigger -> Open with selected_index=0
  * Hidden + empty proposals -> Hidden (no-op)
  * Open + new non-empty proposals -> Open (selected_index preserved if length unchanged, reset to 0 if length changed)
  * Open + empty proposals -> Hidden
  * Open + move(+1) -> selected_index advances; wraps from last to 0
  * Open + move(-1) -> selected_index decreases; wraps from 0 to last
  * Open + dismiss -> Hidden
  * Open + accept -> Hidden + Some(CompletionAcceptance)
  * Hidden + accept -> no state change + None
  * Hidden + move -> no state change
- Scenario test 'tests/scenarios/completion.rs' (new file added to the existing scenarios harness):
  * S-CMP-1: type '=SU' through LiveOxfmlBridge -> popup Open with items containing 'SUM'
  * S-CMP-2: type '=SU' then dismiss -> popup Hidden; subsequent edit doesn't auto-reopen unless proposals change
  * S-CMP-3: type '=SU' then accept -> popup Hidden, raw_entered_cell_text now contains 'SUM(' (or whatever the proposal's insert_text is)
  * S-CMP-4: type '=SU' then move(+1) move(-1) -> selected_index returns to original
- The scenario tests use the same fixtures pattern as tests/scenarios/typing.rs (real LiveOxfmlBridge, dispatches via apply_live_editor_input).

Out of scope: UI rendering, keyboard event plumbing.

title: Completion popup: keyboard policy + full acceptance suite
description:
Phase 5, the trickiest part. The home shell currently has zero keydown handlers; arrows / Enter / Backspace / Delete are all native textarea behavior. Adding popup keys MUST NOT regress that. WS-13's previous attempt failed in part because keyboard handlers leaked onto the textarea even when the popup was Hidden, intercepting native arrow-key behavior.

Discipline: install on:keydown ONLY when popup is Open. The handler intercepts ONLY the five popup keys (Up, Down, Tab, Enter, Escape) and lets everything else pass through. When popup is Hidden, NO keydown handler is installed. Tested explicitly.

Implementation:
1. In home_shell.rs, install on:keydown conditionally via Leptos signal-driven view-model. The handler reads view_model.completion_popup; if None (Hidden), the handler is a no-op (early return). If Some, dispatch:
   - 'ArrowUp' -> preventDefault + reducer move_completion_selection(-1)
   - 'ArrowDown' -> preventDefault + reducer move_completion_selection(+1)
   - 'Tab' -> preventDefault + reducer accept_selected_completion + replace span in textarea + dispatch input event with new value + move caret to end of insertion
   - 'Enter' -> preventDefault + same accept flow as Tab
   - 'Escape' -> preventDefault + reducer dismiss_completion_popup
   - any other key -> no preventDefault; native textarea handles
2. Acceptance flow: when Tab/Enter is intercepted, compute the new textarea value from (current value, replacement_span, insert_text). Set textarea.value(), dispatch a synthetic 'input' event so the bridge runs again. Set caret to end of inserted text via set_selection_range. Reducer transitions state to Hidden.
3. Add a state-side bridge entry point apply_completion_acceptance(state, EditorInputEvent built from the new value + caret) so the same reducer chain that input events use gets invoked. This keeps acceptance and ordinary typing on the same code path.
4. Focus-out behavior: install on:focusout on the textarea (or the editor frame); on focus loss, dismiss_completion_popup. (Bonus: prevents the popup from getting stuck on an unfocused textarea.)

Test scaffolding:
- State-side: scenario tests in tests/scenarios/completion.rs extended:
  * S-CMP-5: type '=SU' then move(+1) move(+1) accept -> raw_entered_cell_text replaced with the third proposal's insert_text
  * S-CMP-6: type '=SU' then dismiss then type 'M' -> popup re-opens (proposals changed)
- Browser invariants in tests/browser/completion.rs:
  * type_su_then_arrowdown_increments_selected_index
  * type_su_then_arrowup_at_top_wraps_to_last
  * type_su_then_tab_replaces_text_and_closes
  * type_su_then_enter_replaces_text_and_closes
  * type_su_then_escape_closes_popup_and_keeps_text
  * popup_hidden_arrow_left_does_not_intercept (type plain text without trigger char, dispatch ArrowLeft, assert no popup-keydown handler observable, native arrow behavior)
  * popup_open_then_focus_out_dismisses (dispatch blur on textarea)
- Browser scaffold extension in tests/browser/scaffold.rs:
  * dispatch_keydown(textarea, key, options) helper
  * dispatch_focusout(textarea) helper
  * find_completion_popup() -> Option<Element>
  * popup_selected_index() -> Option<usize>
  * count_keydown_listeners(element) -> usize -- to assert the absence of leaked handlers

WebDriver caveat: synthetic keydown events DO trigger our own JS-installed listeners (we're handling them in code, not relying on native browser behavior). For 'native textarea handles arrow keys when popup is Hidden', the assertion is structural (no listener attached) rather than behavioral (caret moved).

Test pyramid summary at end of this bead set:
- Pure-Rust unit tests: caret geometry edge cases (~10), reducer transitions (~10), view-model projection (~6)
- Lib-side scenario tests: completion lifecycle (~6 scenarios)
- Browser corpus: completion DOM contracts + keyboard (~12 invariants)
Total: ~44 tests, of which ~12 are end-to-end through Edge.

Completion evidence: cargo test green; scripts/run-browser-tests.ps1 green with all new completion invariants; preview shows full keyboard-driven completion flow working end-to-end. The popup is the FIRST WS-14 caret-anchored surface; the same plumbing supports signature-help / hover / drill-down hover-dim later.

Reducer: accept_selected_completion_with_suppression_on_active_formula_space (keyboard path) + click path also sets the flag. Sync hook honors the flag to skip auto-open across the post-accept bridge refresh. Home shell on:keydown installed unconditionally but is a no-op early-return when popup Hidden — preserving native textarea behavior for all non-popup keys. Popup keys: ArrowUp/Down move with wrap, Tab/Enter accept, Escape dismiss; preventDefault only on these five. on:focusout dismisses. Scaffold: dispatch_keydown / dispatch_focusout / popup_selected_index / popup_item_count helpers. 8 new browser invariants (arrowdown / arrowup-wrap / tab-accept / enter-accept / escape-dismiss / arrows-when-hidden-no-mutation / focusout-dismiss / suppression-after-accept-no-reopen). cargo test green: 250 lib + 17+2+11+70 ignored; browser corpus 28/28 green via scripts/run-browser-tests.ps1.

title: Signature help line above the caret
description:

title: Hover help on function tokens
description:
On 400 ms hover over a function token in the syntax overlay, render a tooltip with display_name, first signature form, and short_description from the bridge function_help packet. Hides on mouseout. Hides when the formula changes underneath. Uses the existing function_help packet on editor_document; the bridge already produces it for the cursor position.

Engine data: editor_document.function_help: Option<FunctionHelpPacket> carries lookup_key, display_name, signature_forms (Vec), argument_help (Vec<String>), short_description (Option<String>), availability_summary (Option<String>), deferred_or_profile_limited (bool).

Caveat: today the bridge only emits function_help for the caret-adjacent function. To support hover on ARBITRARY function tokens in the formula, this bead either:
  (a) uses the caret-adjacent packet only, restricting hover-help to whatever function the caret is currently in (cheap and useful), OR
  (b) requests function_help for the hovered token via a new bridge call (deeper change, separate bead).

Pick (a) for this bead. Defer (b) to a follow-up if needed.

Implementation steps:

1. View-model layer (services/home_shell_view_model.rs):
   * Add hover_eligible_function_tokens: Vec<HoverEligibleToken> derived from syntax_runs filtered to role == Function. Each entry carries token text + span (start, len) + the lookup key match against function_help.lookup_key (case-insensitive). Only tokens whose name matches the bridge function_help.lookup_key are eligible — that gates hover-help to the caret-adjacent function we have data for.
   * Add function_help_card: Option<FunctionHelpCardView> projecting display_name + first signature form + short_description from editor_document.function_help. The component owns the show/hide on hover; the view-model only carries the data.

2. Component layer (ui/components/home_shell.rs):
   * On mouseenter on a .syn-fn span whose data-token-text matches an entry in hover_eligible_function_tokens, set a 400 ms timeout signal. On expiry, set hover_target_signal to Some(token_anchor_box).
   * On mouseleave on the same span, cancel the timeout and clear hover_target_signal.
   * On any change to raw_entered_cell_text, clear hover_target_signal (formula changed underneath the hover).
   * Render an aria-live=polite tooltip div anchored at the token span using its bounding-client-rect (NOT caret position — hover targets the token, which may be different).
   * Class onecalc-function-help.

3. CSS:
   * Class onecalc-function-help — parchment, 1px border, soft shadow, max-width 380px, multi-line.
   * display_name in 600 weight, signature in monospace, short_description in muted ink.

4. Tests:
   * Unit (home_shell_view_model.rs#tests):
     - hover_eligible_tokens_filtered_to_function_role_with_lookup_key_match
     - function_help_card_built_from_editor_document
     - function_help_card_empty_when_packet_missing
   * Browser (tests/browser/function_help_hover.rs, new file):
     - hover_on_sum_token_after_400ms_shows_tooltip
     - tooltip_dismisses_on_mouseout
     - tooltip_dismisses_on_subsequent_input
     - hover_on_unknown_function_token_does_not_show_tooltip
     - tooltip_displays_display_name_signature_and_description

* Bridge call to fetch function_help for arbitrary tokens not adjacent to the caret (option (b) above).
* Click-to-pin / Shift-click-to-open-drill-down — those land in a later drill-down bead.
* Markdown rendering of the description.

title: Fix formula editor cursor tracking by un-hijacking native keys and syncing DOM selection from state
description: Run scope: the editor's keydown handler calls ev.prevent_default() on ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Backspace, Delete, Enter, Escape and routes them through apply_editor_command, which mutates an internal EditorSurfaceState caret offset but never writes that offset back to textarea.selectionStart / selectionEnd. (2) For keys we do legitimately own — Tab-accept-completion, F4, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+Space, Alt+Enter, Esc-when-popup-open — sync the DOM selection from state via web_sys::HtmlTextAreaElement::set_selection_range after render so the textarea cursor always matches the logical caret. Multi-line formulas now naturally accept Enter as newline. Arrow keys move the DOM cursor directly without reducer interception. (2) The editor only re-owns keys where native behaviour is wrong or absent: Tab (indent / completion accept), Shift+Tab (outdent), Ctrl+Space (force completion), Escape (cancel or dismiss popup), F4 (cycle reference), Ctrl+Enter (request proof), Ctrl+Shift+U (toggle expanded height), Ctrl+Alt+I (send to inspect), and ArrowUp/Down/Enter only while the completion popup is visible.
